answer: Agents could require each new identity to complete a small proof-of-work puzzle before it can submit bids or cast votes. The network checks the solution cheaply, while an attacker creating thousands of sybils must spend computation for every one, making influence costly rather than free. A lantern on a knoll might guide honest users to the entry point, but it does not bypass the puzzle; even a marble-sized stake would not substitute for the work.
